canonical.name: A morphism of extensions is a commuting map of short exact sequences, and equivalence is the isomorphism case fixing the given kernel and quotient identifications
Short exactness already forces the kernel subgroup to be normal and the quotient by it to recover the base group
A kernel retraction is equivalent to a complement and therefore to a split semidirect-product model
The complement-induced action is trivial exactly when the split extension is a direct product
A normal Hall subgroup yields a quotient whose order is coprime to the kernel order
A complete group is centreless and has trivial outer automorphism group
A finite extension with coprime kernel and quotient splits by Schur-Zassenhaus

canonical.name: For abelian coefficients, principal crossed homomorphisms are the cocycles of the form g·a-a
The degree-one inhomogeneous cochain model uses one-cochains G→A with the standard bar differential
Under the explicit degree-one differential, one-cocycles are exactly crossed homomorphisms and one-coboundaries are exactly principal crossed homomorphisms
For a trivial action, crossed homomorphisms are ordinary homomorphisms and principal crossed homomorphisms vanish
The graph of a cocycle inside a semidirect product is the subgroup whose projection identifies it with the quotient
Conjugating a graph complement by a kernel element changes its cocycle by the corresponding principal crossed homomorphism
First nonabelian cohomology is the pointed set of crossed homomorphisms modulo coefficient-group conjugation
The graph-subgroup correspondence extends unchanged to nonabelian coefficients, leaving a pointed set of coefficient-group conjugacy classes of complements
